agree.reason: The open budget, firm November 2027 date and frank first-time-creator section would reassure this wary backer, but leaving out the refund pledge and the fixed update schedule takes away the guarantees most likely to win over someone who has already lost $85.

honest.reason: It rightly avoids calling the game a 'proven hit', but 'every one comes from someone who sat down and played' says more than the facts carry, and it hides that most of the 23 ratings came from the creator's own convention table.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out a backer count (about 570), shipping (about $5,150), fees ($2,800) and a $2,650 buffer from the given figures, and shows the 1,240 signups as more than twice the backers needed, though it leaves out the 90,000-subscriber reviewer video due in launch week.

right_comparison.reason: It barely compares this campaign with the reader's real alternative, an unproven first-timer like the one that never shipped, beyond saying it has no past campaign to point to.

qualification.reason: The delivery date is specific, but 'updates throughout production' and 'tell you right away' have no schedule and no consequence, and the available full refund if delivery is more than three months late is never offered.

objections.reason: It deals head-on with the first-time-creator worry and the question of where the money goes, but the 'what if it never ships' objection goes unanswered even though the creator's refund commitment would answer it.

fit.reason: It is a well-structured pitch of about 500 words, but it leaves a '[Game Title]' placeholder when the name Lantern Winter was available.
